question: Can discovery-guided scheduling reduce repeated visual inspection while retaining local evidence beyond whole-image representatives?
inputs: Frozen full collection catalog and 129-family census; no encoder, mask or partition recomputation.
policy: Weighted capped coverage: each family contributes at most two distinct parent photos. Weight is (coherence/4)*(1-shortcut_risk/4); these are existing post-discovery adjudications, not discovery labels or probabilities. No r3 support flags are used for planning.
comparators: static sum of family weights without marginal updates
evaluation: r3 core semantic concepts with one and two distinct parent photos (held aside from planner, correlated secondary evidence)
real photo evidence and source duplication inspection
limits: Transductive inspection scheduling; no claim of new-photo inference, field throughput, causal recovery benefit or independent labels. Every baseline has the same eligible photo pool and budget. All 129 families remain in the discovery catalog.
